findings.title: The test checks for errors before the reader thread has finished.
findings.body: The reader thread is started but never kept or joined. Right after the last delete, the main thread sets `deletedAll` and runs `assertThat(caughtExceptions, empty())` straight away. The reader can still be inside a `groups(...)` call at that moment, so an exception from that last read (the one most likely to hit a deleted group) is added after the assertion has already passed. The test can then pass even though the NPE still happens. Keep a reference to the `Thread` and call `join()` (with a timeout) after `deletedAll.set(true)` and before the assertion. This also stops the thread from outliving the test.

held.title: getSubGroupsCount now returns null when a group is deleted concurrently, and callers that unbox it will throw.
held.body: When the underlying group is removed while it is being read, `modelSupplier.get()` returns null, and this method now returns a null `Long`. Any caller that unboxes the result throws a new NPE, for example `group.getSubGroupsCount() > 0` or passing it where a `long` is expected. Setting it on a representation would be fine. I can't see the callers from here. `GroupUtils` also loses 10 lines in this PR, so check that no remaining caller does arithmetic or comparisons on the result. Returning `0L` for a deleted group, or having callers skip groups whose model is gone, would avoid the problem.
